channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: O que der na urna, eu respeito; sempre respeitei a decisão da maioria, afirma Caiado
item.description: Former Goiás governor and PSD presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado said he will respect the election results and that preventing the PT's return to power will be a greater challenge than defeating Lula.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro falta a interrogatório no STF
item.description: Former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP) failed to attend his scheduled interrogation hearing at the STF this afternoon, where he is accused of attempting to coerce the Brazilian judiciary through U.S. government sanctions. His absence was noted by the judges and may carry procedural consequences. His defense has not yet justified the absence.

item.title: Flávio não é líder nacional nem tem vida própria, é delegado de Jair Bolsonaro, diz José Dirceu
item.description: Former minister José Dirceu (PT) stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for president, is not a national leader nor has independent political life, but merely acts as a 'delegate' of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: No STF, Gilmar diz que CPI do Senado comete excessos que podem configurar crime de abuso de autoridade
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Minister Gilmar Mendes stated that the Senate's CPI may be committing excesses that constitute the crime of abuse of authority. He warned that parliamentary investigations must respect constitutional limits and cannot be used as instruments of political persecution. The statement comes amid debates over the role of CPIs in the 2026 electoral context.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro falta a interrogatório marcado pelo STF
item.description: Former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro failed to appear for a scheduled interrogation by the Supreme Federal Court (STF) on Tuesday, April 14, in the criminal case where he is accused of obstruction of justice. His absence may accelerate the proceedings toward the final stages before trial. Eduardo Bolsonaro did not appoint a lawyer and is being represented by the Public Defender's Office of the Union (DPU); he is also accused of attempting to benefit his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, and of plotting measures against Brazil in the United States.

item.title: Dirceu celebra nova pesquisa sobre Lula: “Sabemos fazer eleição”
item.description: Former minister José Dirceu celebrated the Apex/Futura poll showing a narrowed gap of 2.9 percentage points between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical presidential runoff, emphasizing the PT's ability to win elections. He cited the party's electoral history as evidence of its campaign competence.

item.title: Pesquisa mostra como prisão de Ramagem repercutiu nas redes
item.description: The arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL-RJ) by U.S. Immigration Services over irregular status in the country generated 2.5 million social media interactions and over 50,000 Google Trends searches in Brazil within 24 hours, according to Nexus. The case sparked divided opinions: allies claim political persecution, while others celebrated the prospect of extradition, with memes and debates about political asylum. His wife, Rebeca Ramagem, also generated over 5,000 searches in the same period.

item.title: Base governista troca integrantes na CPI do Crime Organizado e esvazia votação de relatório que mira STF
item.description: Government allies replaced two senators on the Senate's Organized Crime CPI with PT-affiliated members, shifting the committee's balance to block Alessandro Vieira's report calling for the indictment of STF ministers and the Prosecutor General. The change, made hours before the vote, secured a majority opposed to the report, which accused Toffoli, Moraes, Mendes, and Gonet of responsibility crimes. Though presented, the report requires committee approval to proceed.

item.title: Eleições 2026: códigos-fonte dos sistemas eleitorais continuam abertos para inspeções
item.description: Since the launch of the Democratic Transparency Cycle - Elections 2026 on October 2, 2025, the source codes of the voting machines and electoral systems have been available for inspection by authorized institutions, reinforcing the Electoral Justice’s commitment to transparency and security. Entities must submit an official letter to the TSE Presidency with at least 10 days’ advance notice, specifying responsible technicians and the duration of their stay for access. During the cycle, participants can monitor system development, raise technical questions, and submit improvement suggestions, which are evaluated by the TSE’s technical team.

item.title: A reação de Dino e Gilmar ao relatório da CPI do Crime Organizado
item.description: Supreme Court ministers Flávio Dino and Gilmar Mendes rejected the report of the Organized Crime CPI, which calls for the indictment of Gilmar Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, and Attorney General Paulo Gonet. Dino stated that the STF has been fighting organized crime and called the report irresponsible for not targeting militias and drug traffickers. Gilmar labeled the proposal arbitrary and without legal basis, accusing the CPI of creating a smokescreen to generate political electoral gains.

item.title: No Planalto, Alcolumbre diz que há limites institucionais sendo rompidos
item.description: The president of the National Congress, Davi Alcolumbre, warned that the Republic's powers are exceeding institutional limits, undermining republican coexistence. He stated that political disputes have devolved into permanent institutional attacks, contaminated by electoral logic, and that disagreements must not turn into continuous aggression.

item.title: Haddad entra em contato com prefeitos e inicia pavimentação de campanha no interior
item.description: Fernando Haddad is intensifying contacts with mayors in São Paulo’s interior to strengthen his gubernatorial pre-campaign, exploiting dissatisfaction with Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. He seeks tacit support from mayors unhappy with reduced funding and neglect of municipalities. To broaden his appeal, Haddad is leveraging the strategic support of Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, who remains well-regarded in the region due to his past governorship.

item.title: Fundações privadas pedem veto de Tarcísio a projeto que cobra taxa das entidades
item.description: The Paulista Association of Foundations has urged São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas to veto a bill that would impose fees on private foundations for oversight activities conducted by the state Public Prosecutor's Office. The associations argue the measure unfairly burdens their operations and could undermine essential services.

item.title: EUA divulga foto de Ramagem sob custódia do ICE
item.description: Former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL), ex-director of Brazil's intelligence agency Abin and sentenced to 16 years in prison for coup plot involvement, was photographed in ICE custody in Florida after being arrested on immigration-related grounds. The image was released by Orange County Corrections and logged in Florida’s database as a mugshot. Although detained in the U.S., the specific Brazilian charges justifying extradition—requested by the Lula government in 2025—have not yet been disclosed.

item.title: Articulação do governo Lula com STF para derrubar relatório troca 2 integrantes de CPI
item.description: The Lula government is coordinating with STF ministers and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to block the report of the Organized Crime CPI, which recommends indicting Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes. The effort aims to prevent the ministers from being investigated for alleged omissions or complicity in organized crime. The maneuver involves institutional pressure and political alliances to nullify the CPI’s impact.

item.title: Assista à sessão da CPI que votará indiciamento de ministros do STF e PGR
item.description: The Organized Crime Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) holds a session this Tuesday (April 14, 2026) to vote on Senator Alessandro Vieira's (MDB-SE) report, which proposes indicting STF Ministers Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes, as well as PGR Paulo Gonet, for alleged obstruction of justice and favoritism toward criminal organizations. The vote takes place amid rising tensions between Brazil's branches of government, with supporters arguing it is necessary to investigate misconduct and critics labeling it an attempt to intimidate the Judiciary.

item.title: Gleisi defende STF depois de CPI pedir indiciamento de ministros
item.description: Gleisi Hoffmann defended the STF as vital to Brazilian democracy, hours after the Organized Crime CPI recommended indicting three Supreme Court justices and the Attorney General. She also opposed reducing penalties for the January 8 attacks, linking it to Lula’s veto of the Dosimetry Bill, which would benefit Bolsonaro. In the same speech, she highlighted achievements from her tenure at the SRI, including income tax exemptions for up to R$5,000, tax reform, and public safety initiatives.

item.title: 'Candidato é Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio é um delegado dele', diz José Dirceu
item.description: José Dirceu stated that Jair Bolsonaro is the true right-wing presidential candidate for 2026, while Flávio Bolsonaro is merely a 'delegate' without independent leadership, representing only the Bolsonarist conservative electorate. He emphasized that opposition to Lula depends solely on Jair Bolsonaro and that Flávio cannot win in the first round without capturing votes from Caiado and Zema, which he deems unlikely. Dirceu also highlighted the strength of the pro-Lula coalition in the Southeast and South, where the right is divided, and dismissed the possibility of Lula not being a candidate.

item.title: Governo e partidos aliados trocam integrantes da CPI do Crime Organizado em ofensiva para enterrar relatório
item.description: The government bloc replaced opposition senators Sergio Moro and Marcos do Val in the Organized Crime CPI with PT allies Beto Faro and Teresa Leitão to block the final report’s vote, which includes indictment requests against STF ministers and the prosecutor-general. The move, formalized shortly before the committee’s conclusion, secured a government majority of at least seven votes in the 11-member panel, according to involved senators.

item.title: José Guimarães assume ministério e fala em "derrotar o fascismo"
item.description: Federal deputy José Guimarães (PT-CE) was sworn in as minister of the Secretariat of Institutional Relations, replacing Gleisi Hoffmann. In his speech, he stressed the need for dialogue with Congress to defeat the far-right and fascism, strengthening democracy. Guimarães emphasized his role in political articulation to advance agendas such as ending the 6x1 work scale, the Public Security PEC, and approving Jorge Messias for the STF.

item.title: José Guimarães é empossado por Lula e diz que governo não dá certo sem diálogo com Congresso
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sworn in Deputy José Guimarães (PT-CE) as the new Minister of Institutional Relations on Tuesday, April 14, 2026. The role is responsible for coordinating political relations between the federal government and the National Congress. Guimarães emphasized that effective governance depends on constructive dialogue with the Legislative Branch.

item.title: CPI do Crime Organizado tem troca de integrantes antes da votação de relatório
item.description: The Senate's Organized Crime CPI had two titular members replaced hours before voting on a report seeking the indictment of STF ministers and the PGR. The substitution of Sergio Moro and Marcos do Val with Beto Faro and Teresa Leitão shifted the committee's balance, potentially creating a majority to reject Alessandro Vieira's report. With committee president Fabiano Contarato holding a tie-breaking vote, the session began at 2:20 p.m. on Tuesday.

item.title: Marçal diz que Lula só tem chance de se eleger contra Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Businessman Pablo Marçal (União Brasil) stated that Lula would only have a chance to win the 2026 presidential election if running against Jair Bolsonaro, who is currently ineligible and convicted for attempting a coup. Marçal claimed Lula would struggle to defeat Flávio Bolsonaro and suggested the president might be working to release Bolsonaro as an electoral strategy.

item.title: Defesa Civil terá oito novos radares meteorológicos para atuar na prevenção de eventos climáticos extremos
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas announced the acquisition of eight new meteorological radars from USP for São Paulo's Civil Defense, increasing the state's total from 7 to 15 radars, with an investment of R$ 110 million. The total investment package for Civil Defense amounts to R$ 195 million, including risk mapping, prevention works, vehicles, water trucks, and strengthening municipal civil defenses, aiming to improve forecasting and response to extreme weather events.

item.title: Gilmar diz que relatório da CPI do Crime Organizado é 'constrangimento institucional' e defende investigação por abuso de autoridade
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes labeled the Organized Crime CPI report as 'institutional constrangement' and called for an abuse of authority investigation, claiming it seeks political electoral gains and lacks legal basis to indict justices. He directly criticized rapporteur Alessandro Vieira, calling the report a 'true smoke screen' and questioning the CPI's failure to break secrecy on militiamen linked to the Rio operation that left 121 dead. Gilmar also advocated for updating the impeachment law, stating CPIs cannot indict STF ministers.

item.title: Novo Plano Nacional de Educação (PNE): entenda o que é e objetivos
item.description: The new National Education Plan (PNE), to be sanctioned by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on April 14, 2026, sets strategic goals and priorities for Brazilian education from 2026 to 2036, emphasizing learning outcomes, equity, and governance. It proposes a gradual increase in education investment from 7% to 10% of GDP, covering early childhood, basic, vocational, indigenous, rural, quilombola, special, and deaf bilingual education, along with teacher training and the integration of ethnic-racial content across curricula.

item.title: Lula diz que "guerra" contra PCC e CV é do Brasil, não dos EUA
item.description: President Lula stated that the fight against criminal factions PCC and CV is Brazil's sole responsibility, rejecting the U.S. proposal to label them as terrorist organizations, which he views as a pretext for foreign military intervention. He highlighted the approval of the Anti-Gang Law and opened the door for cooperation with the U.S. on narcotics and arms trafficking, provided it respects Brazilian sovereignty.

item.title: Lula sai em defesa do papa Leão XIV e diz que ele ‘não precisa ter medo’ de Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended Pope Leo XIV after criticism from Donald Trump, stating that the pontiff 'does not need to fear' the American leader and praised his stance against the war in Iran. Lula also said Trump chooses between being feared or loved, and that those who fear see not leadership but an oppressor.

item.title: Polêmica com STF sobre visitas a Bolsonaro abre comparação e críticas da oposição
item.description: Bolsonaro’s defense requested STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes to allow Eduardo Torres, a close ally and brother of former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro, to visit him during house arrest, citing personal trust and distrust of external professionals. The STF resisted, questioning Torres’ technical qualifications and upholding strict rules limiting visitors to family, doctors, and lawyers, fearing the house arrest could become a platform for political campaigning. Opposition figures criticize the STF’s perceived severity, while analysts note comparisons to cases like Fernando Collor’s, suggesting possible judicial inconsistency.

item.title: A articulação do PL com Centrão para derrotar o nome do PT ao TCU
item.description: The PL is negotiating with União Brasil, led by deputy Elmar Nascimento, to launch a single candidacy against PT’s Odair Cunha in the TCU ministerial election. The goal is to unite their parliamentary blocs to defeat the PT candidate, who is backed by House Speaker Hugo Motta. If consensus is reached, other Centrão factions are expected to rally behind the chosen nominee to strengthen opposition to the PT.

item.title: TRE condena União Brasil a devolver R$ 1 milhão aos cofres públicos
item.description: The Electoral Court of Rondônia (TRE-RO) ordered the state branch of União Brasil to repay R$ 1 million to public funds due to irregular use of party fund resources in 2022. The ruling cited lack of documentation, generic contracts, and electoral expenses improperly recorded as ordinary costs, amounting to R$ 981,427.17 in irregularities. An additional R$ 2,144.00 of unidentified origin must also be returned.

item.title: Eleitorado 60+ cresce 74% desde 2010 e chega a 36 milhões
item.description: The electorate aged 60 and over grew by 74% between 2010 and 2026, reaching 36.2 million people, reflecting Brazil's accelerated population aging. This group now represents 23.2% of total voters, with the highest concentrations in the South and Southeast regions, led by Rio Grande do Sul (29%), Rio de Janeiro (28%), and Minas Gerais (26%). While voters aged 60-69 show high turnout (85.7% in 2022), those aged 70 and over have low participation (41.1%), although there is a gradual increase in engagement among this older cohort.

item.title: Oposição aciona STF e EUA contra prisão de Ramagem
item.description: The leader of the opposition in the Chamber, Cabo Gilberto (PL-PB), has appealed to the STF, the U.S. Embassy, and the Ministry of Justice to contest the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem (PL-RJ) in Orlando, arguing that the conviction violates a 2025 congressional decision to suspend the criminal case. He requests the suspension of the conviction, annulment of the extradition, and recognition of Ramagem as a political persecuted eligible for asylum in the U.S., labeling the detention as political persecution.

item.title: AGU recorre contra anulação de condenação de aliado de Lula
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (AGU) appealed the decision by Supreme Court Minister Nunes Marques that annulled the conviction of Sergio Gabrielli, former Petrobras president, on grounds of prescription. The AGU argues that prescription was interrupted by the ongoing TCU investigation and notes internal divergence within the STF on the matter. Gabrielli, praised by Lula as 'the most extraordinary Petrobras president of all time', is supporting Lula's 2026 re-election pre-campaign.

item.title: Lula diz que Messias vai dar “conta do recado” no STF
item.description: President Lula stated that Jorge Messias, the Minister of the AGU, is capable and will fulfill the mandate at the STF following his nomination to fill the vacancy left by Luís Roberto Barroso. The documentation was submitted on April 1, initiating Senate review, with a hearing scheduled for April 29 by rapporteur Weverton Rocha, who announced his favorable opinion.

item.title: Gilmar diz que CPI "não tem base legal" para pedir indiciamento de ministros do STF
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes stated that the request for indictment by the Organized Crime CPI against STF ministers and the Attorney General Paulo Gonet lacks legal basis, arguing that only specific bodies like the Senate's Directive Board can process impeachment requests. He also condemned the attempt to criminalize habeas corpus decisions as serious and arbitrary. The final report vote of the CPI is scheduled for this Tuesday afternoon in the Senate.

item.title: Lula elimina dúvida sobre disputar um 4º mandato
item.description: Lula confirmed his candidacy for a fourth term in 2026, citing a moral and ethical commitment to prevent the return of a fascist government, referring to Flávio Bolsonaro as his main adversary. He stated that his re-election would be to propel the country forward, criticized the Bolsonaro government for having destroyed the nation, and declared 2026 as the 'year of truth against lies'. Despite being 80, Lula asserts he is physically and politically fit, citing videos of his physical activity as part of his campaign strategy.

item.title: Eleições 2026: TSE e UNICEF unem forças para que adolescentes tirem primeiro título
item.description: The TSE and UNICEF launched a national partnership to encourage 16- and 17-year-olds to obtain their first voter ID, aiming to boost youth participation in the October elections. The campaign includes intensified social media outreach in April and a challenge for Adolescent Citizenship Nuclei (NUCAs) in over 2,300 municipalities. As of February, only 1.8 million of the 5.8 million eligible adolescents had registered — less than two in ten.

item.title: A reação de Gilmar Mendes ao pedido de indiciamento da CPI do Crime Organizado
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes stated that the request to indict him and two colleagues by the Organized Crime CPI may constitute abuse of authority and should be investigated by the PGR. He criticized the CPI for not focusing on militias and drug traffickers in Rio de Janeiro, claiming the report serves as a 'smokescreen' to attack the STF for electoral gain.

item.title: Lula ironiza Trump e diz que intervenção dos EUA na eleição brasileira o ajudaria
item.description: President Lula ironized the possibility of U.S. intervention in Brazilian elections, suggesting that such interference, if it occurred, might actually help him. His comment followed Donald Trump’s support for Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, whose party recently lost elections in Hungary. Lula used the episode to underscore the ineffectiveness of foreign meddling in democratic processes.

item.title: Alcolumbre diz que país vive momento de 'agressões aos Poderes' e critica quem ultrapassa 'limites institucionais'
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre warned that Brazil is experiencing a moment of 'attacks on the Powers' and criticized those who exceed 'institutional limits', without naming specific targets. His remarks came during the swearing-in of the new Minister of Institutional Relations, José Guimarães, and coincide with the presentation of a Senate Organized Crime CPI report proposing the indictment of three STF ministers and the PGR for responsibility crimes.

item.title: Após CPI pedir indiciamento de três ministros do STF e Gonet, Alcolumbre diz que há 'agressão permanente às instituições'
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre denounced a 'permanent aggression against institutions' following the request to indict three STF ministers (Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli and Gilmar Mendes) and Prosecutor-General Augusto Aras in the final report of the Organized Crime CPI. He stated he will not take action to advance the impeachment process, despite the Senate's authority to judge responsibility crimes. STF ministers criticized the report as politically motivated and flawed, viewing it as part of a broader effort to undermine the Court’s legitimacy.

item.title: Levantamento exclusivo: quem são os partidos que mais investem em candidaturas brancas, pretas e pardas
item.description: TSE data shows that although pardos constitute 45.3% of Brazil’s population, political parties directed nearly two-thirds of the R$ 5.2 billion in public electoral funding in 2022 toward white candidates. PSDB allocated 80.4% of its funds to white candidates, followed by PL (71.6%) and PDT (71.5%). All presidents elected since 2014 identified as white, highlighting a stark racial disparity in Brazil’s highest executive offices despite the country’s majority Black and mixed-race population.

item.title: EUA divulgam foto de Ramagem após ser preso pelo ICE; veja imagem
item.description: Former Brazilian federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem, convicted by the STF for his role in the coup plot and considered a fugitive in Brazil, was detained by ICE in the United States on an immigration hold. His mugshot, showing him wearing a green hoodie, was released by Orange County Jail in Florida. The arrest resulted from international cooperation between Brazil’s Federal Police and U.S. authorities, though no formal charges have yet been disclosed in the U.S. case.

item.title: Sucessão na Alerj: partidos de oposição se manifestam contra nova eleição sem aval do STF
item.description: Opposition parties in Rio de Janeiro, including PSD, MDB, PT, PDT, PSB, Cidadania and PCdoB, united to demand the postponement of the election for the presidency of the Alerj, citing 'institutional disaster and legal uncertainty' following the governor’s impeachment and dual vacancy in the state. They argue that STF preliminary rulings in ADI 7942 and Reclamação nº 92.644/RJ have suspended indirect elections pending final judgment, making a new vote legally unviable at this time.

item.title: Lula queria jantar com senadores nesta quarta, mas agenda de Alcolumbre deixa encontro para depois
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attempted to schedule a dinner with senators for Tuesday (14), but the meeting was postponed due to scheduling conflicts with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. The effort reflected a bid to strengthen Executive-Legislative ties, though tensions between Lula and Alcolumbre persist.

item.title: Relatório de CPI contra ministros do STF pode ter maioria e impõe dilema ao governo
item.description: The report of the Organized Crime CPI proposing the indictment of STF ministers Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes may secure a majority in the committee, according to calculations by government-aligned parliamentarians. This creates a political dilemma for the government, which must balance support for the investigation with the need to avoid institutional conflict with the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: Nova lei aumenta fiscalização sobre clubes formadores de atletas
item.description: Law 15.387/26, signed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, requires sports clubs training athletes to register their programs with the Municipal Council for the Rights of Children and Adolescents. The goal is to strengthen oversight and prevent abusive practices in youth sports training centers. The law originated from Bill 1476/22, introduced by former deputy Milton Coelho (PE).

item.title: O que esperar do TSE sob o comando de indicados por Bolsonaro
item.description: Kassio Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the TSE with André Mendonça as vice, both appointed to the STF by Bolsonaro. TSE ministers believe their conduct will be discreet and non-interventionist, contrasting with Alexandre de Moraes’ leadership in 2022. The current court composition, with more Lula appointees, is expected to generate fewer conflicts in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Trump me ajudaria muito se tentasse interferir nas eleições no Brasil, brinca Lula
item.description: President Lula said he does not fear a possible interference by Donald Trump in Brazil's October elections and even believes it could benefit him in the race against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. He stated that such a scenario might actually help him politically, expressing confidence in his campaign.
